clue.text: Making public announcements diverting as can be

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be made into something else, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds the business of putting out notices as amusing as anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverting' reads as 'amusing', but it and 'as' are the anagram fodder, rearranged under 'can be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising is the trade of publicising products and events through notices to the public.

clue.text: Judge taking part in rare settlement

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in another piece, holding it inside itself
a settlement is an arrangement, so the letters of the word rare are rearranged

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A judge has a hand in an unusual legal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' rearranges RARE as ARER, and 'taking' puts BIT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to decide a dispute, much as a judge does.

clue.text: Set against foreign language poetry

parts.note: set against means versus, abbreviated v
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Poetry is pitted against a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is metrical writing, the stuff poems are made of.

clue.text: Doesn't forget about arms?

parts.note: re means about, concerning
arms are limbs, and limbs are members of the body

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone can recall weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' looks like weapons; here it means limbs, which are members of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to keep it in mind rather than lose it.

clue.text: Greek character involved in a riot-an agitator

indicators.note: the letters are wrapped up within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A Greek man is caught up in street violence started by a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Putting one right, go on about it and cause annoyance

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the scolding word goes around the next piece, surrounding it

parts.note: to go on at someone is to rate or scold them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Correcting someone and nagging them about it is bound to grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IT inside RATE (an old word for scold), giving RITATE after I and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate is to vex or annoy someone.

clue.text: Note water is needed for cereal production

parts.note: G is a musical note
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Farming advice: crops need rainfall to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is the seed harvested from cereal crops such as wheat.

clue.text: A supporter of solid fuel

parts.note: reads like a backer of coal as an energy policy, but describes a metal stand holding logs in a fireplace

explanation.definitionFit: A firedog, or andiron, is one of a pair of iron stands that hold up burning logs in a hearth.

clue.text: Having the same natural gift

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again
native means inborn or natural

explanation.surface: Someone has the same talent they were born with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natural gift' looks like one phrase; 'natural' is wordplay and 'gift' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A donative is a donation or present, especially an official one.

clue.text: Working under pressure indicates impending changes

definitions.text: Working under pressure indicates impending changes

parts.words: Working under pressure indicates impending changes
parts.note: reads like a stressed worker signalling a shake-up, but describes an instrument driven by air pressure that forecasts the weather

explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures atmospheric pressure, and its readings forecast a change in the weather.

clue.text: Love-love in a strange retreat

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as the clue says
to retreat is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rum is an old word for strange
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tryst in an odd hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns RUM into MUR; with A in front that makes AMUR, and 'in' puts O (love, nil) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, borrowed from the French for love.

clue.text: Hamlet upset the girl

indicators.note: something upset is overturned and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Danish prince is troubled by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests the play, where Ophelia upsets the prince; here it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a woman's name, so it stands for a particular girl.

clue.text: Colours, being normal

definitions.meaning: regimental colours are a flag carried into battle

explanation.surface: A flag that is just the usual sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a military flag or banner, and also means the usual level or kind.

clue.text: Rows occasioned by out-moded kitchen equipment

definitions.meaning: rows are lines, as in mountain chains
old cast-iron cooking stoves heated by solid fuel

explanation.surface: Arguments break out over old-fashioned kitchen gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranges are lines or chains of things, and also old-fashioned kitchen stoves.

clue.text: Salesmen should be anonymous

indicators.note: the word should become something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A view that sales staff ought to stay unnamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unnamed has no known identity, which is what anonymous means.

clue.text: Socialist leader listing beastly accommodation

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is taken here

parts.note: tabling is setting out in a table, a way of listing

explanation.surface: A left-wing chief is cataloguing housing fit only for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' sounds like 'nasty', but here it means 'for beasts': housing for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabling is housing for horses and other livestock.

clue.text: Game beauty toting a gun

indicators.note: toting means carrying, so the first word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A lovely woman carrying a firearm is playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toting' puts A GAT inside BELLE: B(AGAT)ELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into holes on a board.

clue.text: Wild duck-a beautiful pink bird

parts.note: flaming means fiercely passionate, wild with feeling
a duck, a score of nothing in cricket, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An angry duck turns out to be a lovely pink bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild duck' looks like one phrase, a kind of bird; split it. In cricket a duck is a batter's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a tall wading bird with rosy plumage.

clue.text: Many a mole is required to make such wear for women

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: the letters are needed to build something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe for a garment that needs a lot of moleskin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mole is' is rearranged under 'required to make' as AMISOLE, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's sleeveless undergarment for the upper body.

clue.text: Starting counting bids for the strongboxes

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is taken here

parts.note: bids are offers, as at an auction

explanation.surface: An auctioneer begins tallying bids for the safes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are chests for keeping money and valuables safe.

clue.text: A repugnant characteristic, that's not disputed

parts.note: greed is an unpleasant trait, one of the deadly sins

explanation.surface: Everyone accepts that someone has an ugly trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed has been settled by all sides, with no argument left.

clue.text: Merit of French translation of 2 down

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: translating changes a thing into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 2 down, the word for poetry

explanation.surface: The worth of a French rendering of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' looks like language talk but rearranges VERSE (the 2 down answer) as SERVE, after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to have earned it.

clue.text: Rant about reform till the end

indicators.note: the word for ranting goes around the next piece

parts.note: to fume is to rage or rant

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A protester rails for change right up to closing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges TILL as LLTI, and 'about' puts it inside FUME.
explanation.definitionFit: Full time is the end of a football match.

clue.text: Provide medical attention-something quite special

definitions.meaning: to care for a patient medically
a delight or indulgence out of the ordinary

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor treats a patient; a treat is also a special pleasure.

clue.text: Standing for a good man at American get-together

parts.note: St, saint, is crossword shorthand for a good man
taken as written
US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: A place is kept for a virtuous man at a US meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is a person's position or rank in society.

clue.text: He wrote 2 down to accommodate a fool

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A poet goes out of their way to put up a simpleton.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 down' points to VERSE: this writer wrote poetry. 'accommodate' puts ASS inside TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet, author of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: A fish month for Jews

parts.note: the bib is a small fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish served in a Jewish month.
explanation.definitionFit: Abib is the old Hebrew name for the first month of the Jewish religious year, later called Nisan.

clue.text: Proceed to prosecute on certain points

indicators.note: one piece comes on, after, the others

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Going ahead with a lawsuit on several counts.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on or come next.

clue.text: Very little drops from this

parts.note: reads as something barely leaking, but means tiny droplets come out of it

explanation.definitionFit: This device turns liquid medicine into a fine mist of tiny droplets for inhaling.

clue.text: Trying to procure foreign currency in great volume

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a tome is a large heavy book
roubles are the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Attempting to get overseas money in large amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like 'attempting' but means difficult. 'in' puts ROUBLE inside TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annoying and hard to deal with is trying.
